fixes.explanation: True, baker. The text says, “Each one threw down his staff, and it became a serpent.” The wise men, sorcerers and magicians did the same things by their magic arts (Exodus 7:11). Staffs turning into serpents, and then more staffs turning into serpents. I would have needed a minute to sit down.

That’s a tidy idea, friend, but the text doesn’t say it. What it says is that Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs (Exodus 7:12). Nobody gets turned back into wood in this verse. Aaron’s staff does the swallowing, and that’s the whole move.
No chase scene in this one, friend. The text says Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs (Exodus 7:12). Nobody is running anywhere in that verse. Sorry to take the action movie away from you.

You got it, baker. “Still, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.” Pharaoh is Egypt’s king, and he had just watched Aaron’s staff swallow up the other staffs. That’s a lot to see and still not listen. I’d have been asking for a replay, and he walked away with his mind already made up.

True, baker. The LORD says, “…take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.” It’s the very same staff that became a serpent in front of Pharaoh. I’d be holding it a little more carefully than usual.

This one is actually true, friend. The LORD tells Moses, “…take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.” So it’s the very same staff that became a serpent before Pharaoh. The one that swallowed up the other staffs is the one he brings.
That’s the first blank, baker. “The fish in the Nile will die…” The LORD says it ahead of time, and then it happens in verse 21. I think this one is heavy, and it’s worth sitting with for a second.

No sons in this scene, friend. The text says Aaron raised the staff and struck the Nile in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials (Exodus 7:20). Pharaoh is Egypt’s king. So the people standing right there are the king’s own officials, front row, no way to say they missed it.

That’s it, baker. “So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river.” All of them, digging. I think that’s a lot of effort for one cup of water.

Rainwater isn’t in the text, friend. It says the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink (Exodus 7:24). The reason is that they could not drink the water from the river. So the verse is about digging, not collecting jars of rain.

No traders show up in this passage, friend. The text says all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink (Exodus 7:24). Buying isn’t mentioned anywhere in the verse. The Egyptians do the digging themselves.
